label: sparse delimiter-step unit, weakly tied to g/x/e/o in prefix
explanation: Active on about 1% of steps. 59% of activation mass falls on the <DEL> step, but only 6.7% of <DEL> steps fire, so phase alone is a poor predictor (F1 0.12). The rest is spread thinly over the original and copy phases: it fires most on input r/1/x, on the step after g/x/e, and in the copy phase when outputting 1/j/a. It never fires at t=0. Delimiter firing becomes more likely when the prefix contains several of g/x/e/o (rate ~17% when 2+ of them appear), but the best simple predicate gets dev F1 ~0.22 and mass recall ~0.38. Larger activations are somewhat more likely to be delimiter steps (coverage rises from 0.42 to 0.63 across quartiles); that is the only magnitude effect I checked. The firing seems to depend on the hidden-state mix of prefix tokens, which the available variables do not capture.
